newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Hagemeyer 1996 profit seen rising 44 pct.
newsitem.headline: Hagemeyer 1996 profit seen rising 44 pct.

text.p: Dutch trading group Hagemeyer NV will next Wednesday announce 1996 profits up by around 44 percent to 279 million guilders, analysts said on Friday.
Analysts expect good organic growth, particularly in southeast Asia where Hagemeyer's trading business was seen growing at 10-15 percent per year.

"The outlook for Hagemeyer is good, especially in the longer run," said analyst Joost Buchner of Van Lanschot Bankiers, noting also that the group had bought out its Hong Kong-based Hagemeyer Cosa Liebermann (HCL) joint venture.
"I see strong growth prospects in southeast Asia," he said.
Analysts said consumer electronics continued to come under pressure, but had probably come through the worst.

"Consumer electronics in the United States is not performing that well," said Herbert Vroon at ING Barings, adding, however, that he was more upbeat on consumer electronics in the Netherlands, with the focus on professional electronics.
"Printers, personal computers and faxes for the professional market are selling well," Vroon said.
He said that Hagemeyer's U.S. speciality food unit, generating up to nine percent of group turnover, was not yet living up to management expectation.
"It's difficult to win market share in this sector," said Vroon, adding that Hagemeyer might think about selling the business in the longer run.
"But new management at that business might also manage to show better results," he said.
Hagemeyer's dividend was likely to increase to 2.25 guilders per share from 2.00 guilders in 1995.
Hong Kong's First Pacific Co has a controlling stake in Hagemeyer.
